narrative.headline: Spain lead at 15.9%, France are second at 10.9% and England fifth at 8.1%. The market signal lifts France and England from the fitted model, but the published curve keeps both below the raw market price. Spain stay first, though Yamal and Williams fitness concerns trim some of the model edge.

france.summary: France are second at 10.9%, with the market signal still well above the fitted model.
france.why: On the published curve, France are about 7.3% in the fitted-model camp and 11.3% in the market-informed camp. Raw de-vigged markets sit much higher, near 16.5%, so the forecast gives that gap partial credit for squad strength and tournament pedigree without following the market all the way.

spain.summary: Spain lead at 15.9%, still first despite Yamal and Williams fitness doubts.
spain.why: Spain remain highest on the fitted-model camp at about 17.6%, while the market-informed camp is nearer 15.2%. Fitness concerns for Yamal and Williams trim the early-group attack case, but Spain remain clear enough across both views to stay top.

england.summary: England are fifth at 8.1%, with the market-informed curve only a little above the fitted model.
england.why: On the published curve, England are about 6.5% in the fitted-model camp and 8.2% in the market-informed camp. The raw market anchor is higher, but the forecast gives it only partial credit for squad depth and a clean training report with Saka available; the later knockout path keeps England behind Spain, France, Portugal and Argentina.

portugal.summary: Portugal are third at 9.5%, with the fitted and market-informed curves close together.
portugal.why: Portugal sit near 8.6% in the fitted-model camp and 9.4% in the market-informed camp. With no material availability news, the published 9.5% stays close to both reads.

argentina.summary: Argentina are fourth at 9.1%, between a stronger fitted-model read and a lower market-informed one.
argentina.why: Argentina are near 9.9% in the fitted-model camp and 8.7% in the market-informed camp. The forecast lands between them, keeping Argentina in the front rank without fully following either side.

brazil.summary: Brazil are sixth at 7.8%, with Neymar's short-term absence not reshaping the title race.
brazil.why: Neymar's calf issue matters for the immediate match context, but its priced title effect is small. Brazil are about 8.4% in the fitted-model camp and 7.4% in the market-informed camp, leaving them just behind England.

germany.summary: Germany are seventh at 7.8%, below the fitted-model read but above the market-informed one.
germany.why: Germany are about 9.5% in the fitted-model camp and 7.1% in the market-informed camp. The forecast recognises Germany's strong model profile without fully dismissing the market's caution.

colombia.summary: Colombia are eighth at 4.6%, with the fitted model doing most of the work.
colombia.why: Colombia sit near 4.6% in the fitted-model camp and 4.4% in the market-informed camp. The raw market is more sceptical, but this forecast treats that as caution rather than decisive evidence.

netherlands.summary: Netherlands are ninth at 4.5%, with the fitted and market-informed curves close together.
netherlands.why: After their draw with Japan, the fitted-model and market-informed camps are broadly aligned. With no large fresh adjustment, the published 4.5% is close to both reads.

belgium.summary: Belgium are tenth at 4.1%, close to the fitted model and above a sceptical raw market.
belgium.why: Belgium are about 4.2% in the fitted-model camp and 4.0% in the market-informed camp. The raw market price is lower, but the published forecast gives the fitted model more weight and keeps Belgium outside the main contender group.

quant_findings.summary: Three candidate branches adjudicated and four major gaps reconciled. Spain-Yamal fitness clears the floor; Brazil-Neymar and the Netherlands draw collapse below it. France and England raw market gaps were material, but the published curve later scales the market-informed view back toward the fitted simulation.
findings: Spain-Yamal fitness clears the priced floor: the branch trims Spain attack in the relevant group matches and survives at the submitted weight.
Brazil-Neymar absence collapses below the floor: the title effect of one short-term group-match absence is too small for a separate branch.
France raw market gap is structural: fitted model around 8.1%, raw market around 16.5%, with both market legs agreeing. The published curve only gives this partial credit.

England raw market gap is borderline structural: fitted model around 7.0%, raw market around 10.7%. The published curve shows about 6.5% in the fitted-model camp and 8.2% in the market-informed camp, so the displayed number is 8.1%, not the raw market price.

quant_findings.summary: Day-5 mixture registered with 3 worlds: fitted model, market-informed base and market-informed base with Spain attack trimmed. Published surface: Spain 15.9%, France 10.9%, Portugal 9.5%, Argentina 9.1%, England 8.1%, Brazil 7.8%, Germany 7.8%.
findings: Mixture worlds: fitted model weight 0.1755, market-informed base weight 0.4745, and market-informed plus Yamal fitness doubt weight 0.35.

England treatment: raw market anchor is around 10.7%, but the published curve shows England at 6.5% in the fitted-model camp, 8.2% in the market-informed camp and 8.1% overall. No independent England world is added because the squad-depth signal is already inside the market-informed base.
Spain-Yamal branch: the branch trims Spain attack for matches 38 and 66 and pulls Spain below the pure fitted-model read while leaving Spain first overall.
Brazil-Neymar branch: collapsed below the floor; the short-term absence is not large enough to warrant a separate title world.

agent.market_justification: France has the largest raw market gap: fitted model around 8.0%, raw de-vigged market 16.5%, gap 8.5pp, about 2.5x the floor. The published curve does not follow that raw price all the way: France is about 7.3% in the fitted-model camp, 11.3% in the market-informed camp and 10.9% overall. England has a smaller raw market gap: fitted model around 7.0%, raw de-vigged market 10.7%, gap 3.7pp, about 1.5x the floor. On the published curve England is about 6.5% in the fitted-model camp, 8.2% in the market-informed camp and 8.1% overall. No independent England branch was added because the market-informed worlds already carry the squad-depth signal, and there was no new injury or suspension on June 15. Other model-market disagreements were treated through the same model and market-informed bases rather than as separate team-specific branches.
agent.change_justification: Steelman and resubmission: the main moves versus the frozen baseline are France up, Spain down and a tiny Australia redistribution. The case for the baseline is that Spain's fitted strength is well calibrated to long-run results and France's lower fitted rating may reflect genuine recent weakness. The case for the submitted mixture is that France's raw market gap is the largest in the field, with bookmakers and Polymarket agreeing, while Spain's market signal and the Yamal/Williams fitness branch both pull against the fitted-model lead. The published surface is lower than the submitted market-informed calculation, so the displayed France and England numbers should be read from the published curve, not from the raw market anchors.
